newsitem.title: USA: US Nov spot natgas up with cold, Dec still strong.
newsitem.headline: US Nov spot natgas up with cold, Dec still strong.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for Wednesday delivery were stronger Tuesday, led by cold weather forecasts for the Midwest and Northeast throughout most of the week, sources said.

November gas on the Gulf Coast pipes traded mostly in the high-$3.80s to low-$3.90s, up more than five cents from Monday's levels, as temperatures in the Northeast were expected to drop more than 15 degrees Fahrenheit tonight.
December prices in the Gulf were talked notionally in the mid-$3.80s, up from most bidweek levels.
The anticipated cold snap again had no effect on pricing at the New York city-gate. Prices for Wednesday delivery hovered around $4.40.
In the Appalachian region, November pricing was in the $4.30-4.35 area, while December prices were talked around $4.25.
In the Midcontinent, prices for Wednesday were in the mid-$3.70s to low-$3.80s, as compared to Monday's levels around $3.90.
December prices were talked notionally softer around $3.80, still more than a $1 over November indices.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to moderate by Friday, forecasters said.

In west Texas, Permian prices for Wednesday delivery traded in the high-$3.50s to the low-$3.70s. Traders reported closing deals at Waha in the $3.70s, with the higher-priced deals evident late. December Permian pricing was talked similarly in the low-to-mid $3.60s.
The San Juan market for next month was in the low-$3.60s, up about $1.15 from November's index, traders said.
Pacific Gas and Electric's 1,087 megawatt Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear power unit is expected to resume full service this Friday, a week after its automatic shutdown.
At the southern California border, the November and December markets were for the most part in convergence in the $3.75-3.90 range in light trading.
The softening in the Canadian market has allowed more California buyers to derive their supplies from the Northwest, thereby stopping the draining of Permian and San Juan supplies.
